metadata.title: Epimechanics — Self-Application and Lawvere's Fixed Point Theorem
metadata.description: The thesis that self-application is the single mechanism behind both entity formation and the diagonal phenomena (Cantor, Gödel, halting, Russell, Tarski). The seven core EMech definitions form a self-dual compact closed category, which is exactly the setting where Lawvere''s fixed point theorem applies.
bullets: T(X)·X is self-application, a representation acting on itself
The seven core EMech definitions form a self-dual compact closed category
Lawvere's fixed point theorem applies in exactly this setting
Cantor, Gödel, halting, Russell, Tarski are instances of the same mechanism
Entities (high-ρ_ac representations) are fixed points of the same map
One mechanism generates both diagonal phenomena and entity formation

content.html:
Motivation

This note was prompted by a thread from Anders Sandberg cataloguing "simple truths with deep reasons" (thread link). His list runs through the unified Stokes theorem, the central limit theorem as a renormalization group fixed point, Noether's theorem, Legendre transforms as the tropical limit of Fourier-Laplace, the exponential function via Lie groups, and the family of diagonal arguments (Cantor, Russell, Gödel, Tarski, halting) unified by Lawvere's fixed point theorem.

Two items on Sandberg's list are load-bearing for Epimechanics. Noether's theorem is inherited directly from the Lagrangian commitment. Lawvere's theorem is the deeper structural match, and the rest of this note works out why. The other items (Stokes, CLT as RG, Legendre, exponential) are structurally adjacent and treated in separate notes.

Background: What a Diagonal Argument Is

Cantor wanted to know if the real numbers can be listed. Suppose someone hands you a list claiming to enumerate every real number between 0 and 1. Cantor builds a new number by walking down the diagonal of that list. He takes the first digit of the first number and changes it. He takes the second digit of the second number and changes it. He keeps going. The number he builds disagrees with every number on the list in at least one place, so it cannot be on the list. The list was supposed to be complete. It is not. There are more reals than the naturals can index.

The move is small but it travels. Russell uses it on sets that contain themselves and gets a paradox. Gödel uses it on provability and gets a true statement that the system cannot prove. Turing uses it on programs that predict their own halting behavior and gets a problem no algorithm can solve. Tarski uses it on truth predicates and shows no language can fully describe its own semantics. Each construction picks an object, lets that object refer to itself in some way, and then defines a new object that disagrees with what self-reference predicts. The new object cannot live in the original system. Something has to give.

The shared shape is self-reference followed by a controlled disagreement. Lawvere noticed in 1969 that the shape is not a coincidence. It is one theorem appearing in five costumes.

The Thesis

Self-reference is also what makes an entity an entity. A persistent thing in Epimechanics is a representation XXX such that the dynamics derived from XXX, applied back to XXX, returns something close enough to XXX to count as the same thing. The representation refers to itself through its own dynamics, and the loop closes. This is the same move that Cantor and Gödel exploit, read in the opposite direction. Where the diagonal arguments construct objects that resist self-consistency, entity formation finds objects that achieve it.

The claim in this note is that these are not two phenomena. They are two readings of one mechanism: a representation applied to itself. The central object in Epimechanics, T(X)⋅XT(X) \cdot XT(X)⋅X, is a self-application. The category in which the seven core EMech definitions live is exactly the categorical setting where Lawvere's fixed point theorem applies. The theorem then governs both readings at once. The fixed points it locates are entities. The fixed points it forbids are the diagonal obstructions.

The rest of this note works out the consequences.

The Mechanism

A representation XXX can act as both operator and operand. Write the self-application as

X′=T(X)⋅XX' = T(X) \cdot XX′=T(X)⋅X

Iterating this map has three possible asymptotic regimes:

  1. Decay. X′→0X' \to 0X′→0 or to a trivial representation. The candidate dissolves.
  2. Drift. X′X'X′ wanders without settling. No persistent representation forms.
  3. Fixed point. X′≈XX' \approx XX′≈X under the loop dynamics. A persistent representation forms.

The third case is what ρ_ac measures at the loop level. An entity is a fixed point of self-application, evaluated over a closed loop. See coupling_chains.md and 01_5_causors.md for the dynamics; this note states the categorical structure underneath.

The Category

The seven core EMech definitions (representation, transformation, coupling, loop, persistence, entity, computation) form a self-dual compact closed category. Self-dual means every object has a dual that is itself up to canonical isomorphism: a representation can be read as an operator on representations and vice versa. Compact closed means there is enough structure (unit, counit, internal hom) for objects to apply to one another inside the category.

This is the categorical setting in which Lawvere's fixed point theorem holds. The conditions are not imported; they are forced by the definitions.

Lawvere's Theorem

Lawvere (1969) proved that in a cartesian closed category, if there exists a point-surjective map f:A→BAf: A \to B^Af:A→BA, then every endomorphism g:B→Bg: B \to Bg:B→B has a fixed point. The contrapositive is the workhorse: if there is an endomorphism ggg with no fixed point, then no point-surjection A→BAA \to B^AA→BA exists.

Cantor's diagonal, Russell's paradox, Gödel's incompleteness, Tarski's undefinability of truth, and the halting problem are all instances of the contrapositive. Each construction picks an endomorphism ggg with no fixed point (boolean negation, "this sentence is not provable", "this program does not halt", "this set is not a member of itself") and concludes that the relevant point-surjection cannot exist. Yanofsky (2003) showed that this scheme covers a wider class, including paradoxes in computability theory, complexity theory, and formal language theory, all from the same diagram chase. A recent survey (Barreto, 2025) collects the modern proofs and the categorical refinements since Lawvere's original paper.

Lawvere's original setting is cartesian closed. Epimechanics needs a slightly stronger setting, because the dynamical reading of T(X)⋅XT(X) \cdot XT(X)⋅X requires that representations be applicable in both directions, not just from AAA to BAB^ABA. This is the compact closed extension, where every object has a dual and the category is equivalent to its opposite (Kelly and Laplaza, 1980; Selinger, various). Compact closed categories are also the standard setting for categorical quantum mechanics (Abramsky and Coecke, 2004), which is encouraging for a framework that hopes to recover quantum behavior from event-layer structure.

In the compact closed setting the same theorem runs in both directions. The presence of fixed points (entities) and the absence of total point-surjections (incompleteness, undecidability) are two faces of the same self-application structure.

Why Both Follow

Diagonal phenomena and entity formation are dual readings of the same map T(X)⋅XT(X) \cdot XT(X)⋅X:

ReadingObject of interestLawvere consequence
Logical / syntacticEndomorphism without fixed pointNo total surjection (Cantor, Gödel, halting)
Dynamic / physicalSelf-application with fixed pointPersistent representation (entity)

The logical readings construct a ggg that resists fixed points. The dynamic readings find the XXX that survives the iteration. Both live in the same category, governed by the same theorem.

This is why diagonal phenomena are not pathologies of formal systems. They are the negative space of entity formation. Wherever self-application is possible, both readings are forced.

Consequences for the Framework

  1. The Lagrangian commitment is justified categorically. A Lagrangian formulation requires that the state act on itself through a variational principle. Self-dual compact closed structure is the minimal categorical assumption for this to be coherent. Calling the Lagrangian "the strongest structural postulate" (per 00_prelude.md) is a statement that EMech commits to this category.

  2. ρ_ac is a fixed-point indicator. Whatever measure of persistence is used, it should reduce to "how close is T(X)⋅XT(X) \cdot XT(X)⋅X to XXX under loop dynamics." Definitions of ρ_ac that drift from this miss the categorical anchor.

  3. Open question: closed but not exact entities. Lawvere's theorem locates fixed points but does not classify them. Some fixed points may be reachable from a smaller substrate (exact); others may be locally consistent but globally obstructed (closed but not exact). This distinction has a counterpart in de Rham cohomology and should be made precise for entity classification. Tracked in 05_ontology_and_open_questions.md.

  4. Computation is producing a representation. Self-application is computation in the EMech sense: the act of T(X)T(X)T(X) on XXX yields a new representation X′X'X′. Lawvere's theorem then says that any sufficiently expressive computation must either have fixed points (produce stable outputs that refer to themselves) or admit diagonal obstructions (problems it cannot decide). Both regimes are observed.

What This Note Does Not Claim

It does not claim that every diagonal argument is "really" an entity, or that every entity is "really" a diagonal proof. The claim is weaker and more precise: both phenomena live in the same category and are governed by the same theorem. The substantive work of identifying which fixed points are entities (rather than artifacts) and which diagonal constructions are informative (rather than trivial) is not done by Lawvere's theorem. It is done by the dynamics of T(X)⋅XT(X) \cdot XT(X)⋅X under loop coupling, which is the rest of Epimechanics.

References

Primary sources on Lawvere's theorem and its scope

  • Lawvere, F. W. (1969). Diagonal Arguments and Cartesian Closed Categories. Lecture Notes in Mathematics 92, Springer. Reprinted in Reprints in Theory and Applications of Categories 15 (2006).
  • Yanofsky, N. S. (2003). A Universal Approach to Self-Referential Paradoxes, Incompleteness and Fixed Points. Bulletin of Symbolic Logic 9(3), 362-386. arxiv:math/0305282. Shows that Cantor, Russell, Gödel, Tarski, halting, and a wider family of paradoxes share one categorical scheme.
  • Barreto, J. R. (2025). A Survey on Lawvere's Fixed-Point Theorem. arxiv:2503.13536. Modern proofs, applications to fixed-point combinators, type theory, and homotopy type theory.
  • nLab entry: Lawvere's fixed point theorem.

Compact closed and self-dual category structure

  • Kelly, G. M. and Laplaza, M. L. (1980). Coherence for compact closed categories. Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 19, 193-213.
  • Abramsky, S. and Coecke, B. (2004). A categorical semantics of quantum protocols. LICS 2004. The standard reference for compact closed categories in physical reasoning.
  • nLab entry: compact closed category.

Proximate motivation

  • Sandberg, A. (2026). Thread on simple truths with deep reasons. x.com/anderssandberg/status/2053757849918939364.

Related theory notes in this repo

  • coupling_chains.md, 01_5_causors.md, 02_meta_entities.md, 05_ontology_and_open_questions.md.

metadata.title: Epimechanics Application: Companies as Auto-Causal Entities
metadata.description: Companies are not merely alive: they are auto-causal meta-entities with bonds, loops, and keystones. Epimechanics provides the grammar for reading their causal structure, predicting their dynamics, and understanding why the genome metaphor finally works.

bullets.Companies satisfy all three meta-entity: causal emergence (Hoel), near-decomposability (Simon), and synergistic behavior (Daniels/Krakauer/Flack)

bullets: The "genome" metaphor becomes load-bearing when recast as the company's complete bond-loop structure in Q1-Q5 parameter space

bullets.Two forces are making the implicit bond: agentic AI (can execute judgment-laden instructions) and regulatory pressure (audit demands a manifest)

bullets: Companies exist across three coupled substrates (physical, informational, and mimetic), and persist only while the coupling tensor $\Gamma_{ij}$ maintains coherence

bullets.The framework predicts that companies, l: high $\rho_{\text{ac}}$ enables persistence but increases attack surface density

coverImage.alt: A luminous corporate meta-entity rendered as a dense bond-loop network: silhouetted figures and documents linked by glowing causal loops that fold back on themselves, forming a coherent boundary around a self-sustaining organizational whole. Three coupled substrates (physical bodies, informational artifacts, and shared mimetic patterns) appear as overlaid translucent layers, with golden coupling lines binding them into one auto-causal organism on a dark backdrop.

content.html:
In plain English: Companies are meta-entities: causal structures that exist across people, documents, and shared patterns, with their own state variables, coupling tensors, and persistence dynamics. The biological analogy (companies are "alive," companies have "genes") has always been intuitive but formally vague. Epimechanics makes it precise: a company is a bond-loop configuration that satisfies the conditions for causal emergence. The genome is the complete set of bonds and loops. Expression is which loops fire under which conditions. And that structure is now becoming readable and writable.

The Old Intuition and Why It Failed

For two hundred years, we studied companies the way pre-Mendel biologists studied animals: by their phenotype. We could see the body: the org chart, the workflows, the outputs, the building. We could observe behavior. But the instructions that produced all of it lived somewhere we couldn't read.

The most valuable causal structure in every company has always been the structure nobody wrote down. It sat in founders' heads, in tribal knowledge passed across cubicles, in undocumented processes, in Slack threads no new hire would ever find. You could acquire a company and not actually possess its bond-loop structure; only its expression in the people who happened to be there that quarter.

The biological metaphor persisted because something real was being pointed at. But the metaphor couldn't do work because it had no formal grounding. "DNA" and "genes" and "organism" were gestures toward a structure that couldn't be specified, measured, or manipulated. The intuition was correct; the vocabulary was borrowed from the wrong level.

Why Now: Two Simultaneous Pressures

Two things are changing simultaneously.

The first is that we've finally built tools that can execute bonds of the messy, judgment-laden kind that companies actually run on. The instructions don't have to compile down to a deterministic if-then anymore. They can read context, exercise discretion, recover from ambiguity. The kind of causal patterns a company actually contains (here's how we handle an unhappy customer who's been with us for years, here's when to escalate vs. resolve, here's what counts as a clean handoff) is finally encodable in a form a machine can act on.

In Epimechanics terms: the coupling tensor TinstructionactionT^{\text{action}}_{\text{instruction}}Tinstructionaction​ between written instructions and actual behavior used to be near-zero for all but the simplest operations. Humans were required as interpreters, as transducers converting informal instructions into contextual action. Agentic AI raises TinstructionactionT^{\text{action}}_{\text{instruction}}Tinstructionaction​ toward unity for increasingly complex instruction types. The bond from "instruction" to "action" is becoming direct.

The second is that the regulatory environment, almost everywhere it touches sensitive work, is making the unwritten structure legally hostile. You cannot run a HIPAA-covered practice on tribal knowledge anymore. You cannot run a financial workflow on what the senior person happens to remember. The unwritten parts have to become written parts. Audit demands a manifest.

In Epimechanics terms: external coupling pressure (regulatory field Φcompliance\Phi_{\text{compliance}}Φcompliance​) is forcing the informational substrate to expand. Patterns that existed only in the mimetic substrate (person-to-person transmission) must migrate to the informational substrate (documented protocols). The coupling among substrates is being restructured by external force.

Together, these two pressures mean that companies now have an explicit, readable, and increasingly writable bond-loop structure, something they did not have before.

Companies as Meta-Entities: The Formal Claim

Part 2 established when an aggregate earns its own state variable XXX. Three criteria must be satisfied:

CriterionSourceTest
Causal emergenceHoel, Albantakis & Tononi (2013)EI(macro)>EI(micro)EI(\text{macro}) > EI(\text{micro})EI(macro)>EI(micro): the company-level description captures more causal structure than the employee-level description
Near-decomposabilitySimon (1962)Within-company coupling ≫\gg≫ between-company coupling: employees interact more with each other than with external parties
Synergistic behaviorDaniels, Krakauer & Flack (2016)Collective output is not decomposable into sum of individual outputs: the company does things no individual could

Most companies satisfy all three. The macro-level description of "the company's strategy" or "the company's culture" captures causal structure that no description of individual employees provides (Hoel). The tight internal coupling of daily collaboration, shared context, and mutual dependency far exceeds the loose external coupling of occasional customer or vendor interaction (Simon). And the collective output (a product, a service, a market position) is synergistic: it contains information not present in any linear combination of individual contributions (Daniels et al.).

The company is therefore a genuine entity in Epimechanics' sense: it has its own state variable XcompanyX_{\text{company}}Xcompany​, its own generalized mass Mcompany\mathcal{M}_{\text{company}}Mcompany​ (total causal content), its own auto-causal density ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​ (self-sustaining loop strength), and its own coupling tensor TijT^i{}_jTij​ to external fields.

Three Substrates: Where Companies Exist

Like all meta-entities, a company exists simultaneously across three substrates:

Physical Substrate

The embodied layer: employees, offices, servers, inventory, equipment. A company's physical substrate is its instantiation in matter: the atoms that carry its patterns. This is what you see when you visit the office or shake hands with the CEO.

The physical substrate is causally necessary but not sufficient. You can destroy the physical substrate (fire everyone, demolish the building) and the company can survive, so long as the informational and mimetic substrates remain intact elsewhere. You can preserve the physical substrate (keep everyone employed) and the company can dissolve, if the bonds that coordinated their activity are severed.

Informational Substrate

The encoded layer: contracts, codebases, process documents, org charts, legal filings, institutional memory systems. This is what persists when individual employees leave. A well-documented company can lose its entire workforce and reconstitute itself from its informational substrate (with sufficient new physical instantiation).

The informational substrate is what M&A due diligence attempts to audit. Acquiring a company means acquiring its informational substrate: the encoded patterns that, when instantiated in new physical carriers, will reproduce the company's behavior. The gap between "what we thought we were buying" and "what we actually bought" is often a gap in informational substrate fidelity.

Mimetic Substrate

The self-reproducing conceptual layer: culture, values, unwritten norms, "how we do things here," the patterns that propagate from employee to employee through imitation and socialization rather than documentation. This is what onboarding transmits that no document captures.

The mimetic substrate is the hardest to transfer and the easiest to lose. It exists only in the minds of current practitioners and in the social dynamics among them. It cannot be downloaded. When key culture-carriers leave, the mimetic substrate degrades, and no amount of documentation can fully replace it.

The Coupling Tensor Γij\Gamma_{ij}Γij​

The company's causal power derives not from any single substrate but from the coupling among all three. Define the inter-substrate coupling tensor:

Γij=coupling strength between substrate i and substrate j\Gamma_{ij} = \text{coupling strength between substrate } i \text{ and substrate } jΓij​=coupling strength between substrate i and substrate j

The company persists as a coherent entity when λmin⁡(Γ)>κc\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma) > \kappa_cλmin​(Γ)>κc​: when the minimum eigenvalue of the coupling tensor exceeds the critical coherence threshold. Drop below this threshold and the substrates decouple: documents no longer guide behavior, culture no longer propagates, physical presence no longer constitutes participation. The entity dissolves not because any substrate vanished but because they stopped reinforcing each other.

The Bond-Loop Structure: What a Company Is Made Of

Part 1.5 defines the structural primitives: bonds (recurring causal patterns connecting state variables) and loops (closed compositions of bonds that regenerate their own conditions). This is the vocabulary that makes the "genome" metaphor precise.

Bonds as Organizational Primitives

A bond in a company is a recurring causal pattern: how we log a privileged access event, how we onboard a new patient, how we close out a deal. Each bond is characterized by:

PropertyMeaning
DirectionWhich state variables connect (e.g., "customer complaint" → "resolution action")
Strength σb\sigma_bσb​Resistance to dissolution (how hard is it to change this process?)
Latency τb\tau_bτb​Time between input and output (how fast does this process fire?)
Reliability rbr_brb​Probability the pattern fires when activated (how consistently does this work?)

The Q1-Q5 descriptors from Part 1.5 characterize each bond:

  • Q1 (Energy mode): Does this bond store capacity (potential) or drive immediate action (kinetic)?
  • Q2 (Output target): Does it connect to another bond (gating), to state directly (action), or to a loop (enabling)?
  • Q3 (Topology): Is it part of a closed loop or an open chain?
  • Q4 (Leverage Λ\LambdaΛ): How much output per unit input? (High-leverage bonds are management decisions; low-leverage bonds are routine operations)
  • Q5 (Timescale): Fast relative to the company's operating cycle (regulators) or slow (structural)?

Loops as Auto-Causal Structure

A loop is a closed composition of bonds: a causal cycle where the output of the last bond feeds back to the input of the first:

L:    Xi1→b1Xi2→b2⋯→bn−1Xin→bnXi1↺\mathcal{L}: \;\; X_{i_1} \xrightarrow{b_1} X_{i_2} \xrightarrow{b_2} \cdots \xrightarrow{b_{n-1}} X_{i_n} \xrightarrow{b_n} X_{i_1} \quad \circlearrowleftL:Xi1​​b1​​Xi2​​b2​​⋯bn−1​​Xin​​bn​​Xi1​​↺

Loops are where ρac>0\rho_{\text{ac}} > 0ρac​>0 emerges. A company's core loops include:

LoopDescriptionFailure mode
Revenue loopCustomer → product/service → payment → reinvestment → customerRevenue falls below operating cost
Hiring loopNeed → recruit → onboard → productive employee → identify needTalent pipeline breaks; knowledge loss
Product loopMarket signal → development → release → feedback → iterationProduct stagnates; market fit lost
Culture loopNorm → behavior → reinforcement → transmission → normCulture carriers leave; drift
Compliance loopRegulation → process → audit → adjustment → complianceRegulatory failure; legal exposure

Each loop has its own ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​ contribution. The company's overall auto-causal density is the integrated effect of all loops. The key point is that ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​ is not the sum of individual loop strengths. It is a system-level property that emerges from loop coupling. Loops that reinforce each other (positive κsys\kappa_{\text{sys}}κsys​) contribute more than their individual strength; loops that compete or drain each other (negative κsys\kappa_{\text{sys}}κsys​) contribute less.

The "Genome": Complete Bond-Loop Manifest

The genome of a company, precisely stated, is the complete specification of its bond-loop structure:

  • All bonds, with their Q1-Q5 coordinates
  • All loops, with their composition and coupling
  • The coupling tensor TijT^i{}_jTij​ relating the company to external fields
  • The inter-substrate coupling tensor Γij\Gamma_{ij}Γij​

This is what tribal knowledge was always encoding implicitly. This is what AI execution and regulatory pressure are forcing to become explicit. The genome was always there; we just couldn't read it.

Gene Expression: Conditional Loop Activation

Not all loops run all the time. Expression is what happens when a particular situation activates a particular loop:

  • A customer complaint arrives → the service recovery loop fires
  • A regulation comes into force → the compliance adjustment loop fires
  • A new hire's first day begins → the onboarding loop fires

The genome doesn't execute all at once. The environment (market conditions, regulatory state, internal triggers) determines which loops express. A dormant loop still exists (it is part of the bond-loop structure), but it contributes nothing to ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​ until activated.

This is why companies can appear to change dramatically without their deeper structure changing. A recession activates loops (cost-cutting, layoffs, defensive positioning) that were always present but dormant. The genome didn't change; the expression pattern did.

Timescales of Change: Development, Adaptation, Evolution

Companies change on three different clocks. Conflating them is one of the most common mistakes in how people talk about organizational change.

Development (One Entity, One Lifetime)

A new company begins as something like a fertilized cell: a small core of instructions with enormous latent capacity. As it grows, it differentiates. New loops express. New bonds come online. New specializations emerge.

The genome doesn't change much during development; what changes is which parts of it are being expressed and at what scale. Most of what people call "scaling" is actually development: the progressive expression of latent organizational capacity under environmental conditions that call for growth.

Adaptation (One Entity, Environmental Response)

A new regulation comes into force. A market shifts. A competitor changes the local fitness landscape. The company edits its own bond-loop structure in response.

Adaptations propose themselves; some are accepted, some rejected; the manifest itself mutates. A healthy company adapts continuously and at low cost; its bonds are strong enough to persist but not so rigid that they can't be modified. An unhealthy company waits until adaptation is forced on it, and then experiences it as crisis.

In Epimechanics terms: the company's ΔV\Delta VΔV (stability basin depth) determines how large an environmental perturbation it can absorb without crossing a dissolution threshold. High ΔV\Delta VΔV means the company can tolerate significant environmental shifts without losing loop integrity. Low ΔV\Delta VΔV means small perturbations cascade into structural damage.

Evolution (Across Populations, Across Generations)

Successful patterns spread. Templates get forked, modified, propagated. The bond-loop structures that survive in one niche become the canonical structure for that niche, until something better emerges or the niche itself changes.

This is selection acting at the level of the species, and it is the timescale on which industries (not individual firms) actually transform.

Companies as Species: The Gene Pool

A dental practice in one town and a dental practice in another are not the same entity, but they share enormous amounts of bond-loop structure. A real estate brokerage, a small accounting firm, a clinical trial site: each of these is a niche, and each niche has converged on a characteristic genome that lets entities survive there.

The genome of "dental practice" includes:

  • Patient intake loop
  • Insurance verification bonds
  • Recall scheduling loop
  • Clinical documentation bonds
  • Billing loop
  • Compliance bonds (state dental board coupling)

Two practices will differ at the margins (different employees, different local market conditions, different histories), but they share a core that is more conserved than any individual founder appreciates.

This is what makes the species frame useful. A new dental practice does not need to work out its genome from scratch. It can inherit. It can fork. It can specialize where its environment differs.

And once you can think in species, you can think in gene pools: the shared library of bond-loop structures across all entities of a kind, from which any new entity can draw and into which the successful innovations of any individual entity can flow back. The niche, not the firm, is where the deepest learning accumulates.

Structural Vulnerability: The Keystone Problem

Part 2.5 established that auto-causal entities face a fundamental tension: the loops that sustain them become amplification engines if a keystone bond is perturbed.

Keystone Bonds in Companies

Not all bonds contribute equally to a company's loop structure. Some are keystones: their integrity is required for loops to function. Remove them and the loop collapses:

κb=ΔρacΔσb\kappa_b = \frac{\Delta \rho_{\text{ac}}}{\Delta \sigma_b}κb​=Δσb​Δρac​​

A bond with high κb\kappa_bκb​ is load-bearing. Small reductions in its strength cause large drops in loop integrity.

Examples of keystone bonds in companies:

KeystoneLoop it supportsFailure cascade
Founder's knowledgeProduct development loopProduct stagnates without irreplaceable context
Key customer relationshipRevenue loopRevenue concentration → single point of failure
Compliance officer expertiseCompliance loopRegulatory exposure when expertise leaves
Cultural anchor (early employee)Culture loopCulture drift when anchor departs
Core technology patentProduct protection loopCompetitive exposure when patent expires

Attack Surface Density

The same property that makes a company capable (high ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​) also makes it vulnerable to intelligent disruption:

ρattack(∂E)=∑b∈∂Eκb⋅ρac(Lb)\rho_{\text{attack}}(\partial E) = \sum_{b \in \partial E} \kappa_b \cdot \rho_{\text{ac}}(\mathcal{L}_b)ρattack​(∂E)=∑b∈∂E​κb​⋅ρac​(Lb​)

where the sum is over keystone bonds accessible at the company's boundary.

A company with powerful loops (high ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​) and accessible keystones (keystone bonds reachable from outside) has high attack surface density. Competitors, regulators, or adverse circumstances that target these keystones can trigger dissolution cascades with minimal force expenditure.

This is why companies die. Not usually because they run out of resources (brute force dissolution), but because a keystone bond fails and the loop that depended on it collapses, and that loop's failure cascades to other loops through the coupling structure. The company's own auto-causal machinery amplifies the perturbation.

Where the Frame Stretches: Notes on the Analogy

Workers Are Not Proteins

The mapping between workers and proteins is loose. A protein is a specific folded molecule that performs one job, dumbly and reliably. The workers a modern company expresses (human or machine) carry far more reasoning than that. The cleaner analogue is probably a small specialized cell, or even an organelle, rather than a single protein.

This is a place where the biological analogy needs to be calibrated, not abandoned. The Epimechanics primitives (bonds, loops, keystones, coupling tensors) carry across cleanly; it is only the specific cellular vocabulary that has to shift to a coarser grain.

What This Predicts

Epimechanics stands or falls on its predictions. Three testable claims follow from this analysis:

1. Explicit genome → higher M&A success rate

If the bond-loop structure is made explicit and auditable, acquirers should be able to assess what they're actually buying. The prediction: companies with documented bond-loop structure (not just process documentation, but explicit loop topology with keystone identification) should have higher post-acquisition integration success rates than companies with equivalent financials but undocumented structure.

Test: Compare M&A outcomes for acquisitions where explicit operational playbooks existed vs. where they didn't, controlling for financial metrics. The framework predicts a measurable difference in integration success.

2. Keystone identification → targeted resilience

If keystones can be identified, companies should be able to invest in redundancy specifically at high-κb\kappa_bκb​ positions. The prediction: companies that explicitly identify and harden keystones should show higher resilience to targeted disruptions (key person departure, regulatory change, competitive attack) than companies that invest equivalent resources uniformly.

Test: Survey companies on whether they have explicit keystone identification and redundancy practices. Correlate with survival rates under measured disruption events.

3. Inter-substrate coupling as a leading indicator

If the coupling tensor Γij\Gamma_{ij}Γij​ among substrates (physical, informational, mimetic) determines entity coherence, then degradation of this coupling should predict entity dissolution before traditional financial metrics do. The prediction: measurable decoupling among substrates (e.g., documented processes that no one follows, culture that contradicts stated values, physical presence that doesn't constitute participation) should lead financial distress by a measurable interval.

Test: Develop metrics for inter-substrate coupling (process adherence, culture-values alignment, participation intensity). Test whether coupling degradation precedes financial degradation in failing companies.

Closing

The bond-loop structure was always there. The auto-causal density was always what distinguished companies that persist from companies that dissolve. The coupling among substrates was always what gave companies their causal power.

We just couldn't read it. Now we can, and that changes what it means to run a company.

The genome metaphor was never wrong. It was just waiting for a vocabulary that could make it precise. Bonds, loops, keystones, coupling tensors, auto-causal density, attack surface, substrate coupling: these are the primitives. From them, you can derive what kind of entity you're looking at, what makes it persist, and what would make it dissolve.

The grammar is Epimechanics. The vocabulary is domain-specific. The measurement is empirical. And the test is whether the predictions hold.

metadata.title: Epimechanics — Part 0b: The Event Layer
metadata.description: The foundation beneath physics. The causal event primitive, the cause-plex, and the three structural properties from which spacetime, energy, and quantum mechanics emerge. No physics is assumed — physics is derived.
bullets: The primitive is the causal event — a state transition with no assumed physics
The cause-plex is the hypergraph of all causal events with their partial ordering

content.html:
In plain English: Before energy, before spacetime, before particles — there is causation. One thing leads to another. That's it. Causal set theory (not us) showed that spacetime geometry can be derived from causal structure — this is established physics. Noether's theorem (standard physics) shows energy emerges from symmetry. Quantum mechanics from multiway structure is a research program, not a completed derivation. This document summarizes the causal foundation and points to where the established results come from.

The Primitive: The Causal Event

The most fundamental thing in the framework is not energy, not spacetime, not a particle. It is the causal event — a state transition:

e:Si→Sje: \mathcal{S}_i \to \mathcal{S}_je:Si​→Sj​

One configuration follows from another. No energy assumed. No time assumed. No space assumed. Just the "follows from" relation between states.

Consider a candle flame. The heat from the burning wax vaporizes more wax, which feeds the flame, which produces more heat. Each step is a state transition: one configuration of molecules produces the next. No energy concept is needed to describe this chain — just "this state follows from that one."

In cause-plex notation, the flame is four causal events forming a loop:

Events e1,e2,e3e_1, e_2, e_3e1​,e2​,e3​ form a closed causal loop — each event's output enables the next. Event e4e_4e4​ (air turbulence elsewhere in the room) has no causal path to or from the flame's core loop — it is causally disconnected (P2 applies: their order doesn't matter to the outcome).

This is the same starting point as Wolfram's ruliad: an abstract hypergraph of state transitions. The cause-plex is the specific subgraph realized by the physical world.

The Cause-Plex

The cause-plex C\mathcal{C}C is the hypergraph of all causal events with their partial ordering:

C=(E,≺)\mathcal{C} = (E, \prec)C=(E,≺)

where:

  • EEE is the set of all causal events
  • ≺\prec≺ is the "precedes" relation (strict partial order)

The cause-plex carries no physics by assumption.

Three Properties

The cause-plex has three structural properties. Causal set theory has shown that spacetime geometry follows from these (Malament's theorem). Energy from symmetry is standard physics (Noether). QM from multiway is a research program.

P1: Causal Partial Ordering

Already encoded in (E,≺)(E, \prec)(E,≺):

  • Irreflexive: No event precedes itself
  • Transitive: If e1≺e2e_1 \prec e_2e1​≺e2​ and e2≺e3e_2 \prec e_3e2​≺e3​ then e1≺e3e_1 \prec e_3e1​≺e3​
  • Asymmetric: If e1≺e2e_1 \prec e_2e1​≺e2​ then not e2≺e1e_2 \prec e_1e2​≺e1​

This is the minimal structure for "causation" to mean anything. It defines what "before" and "after" mean — not in time (time doesn't exist yet), but in the causal ordering itself.

P2: Causal Invariance

Events with no causal path between them — causally disconnected events — commute:

e1⊥e2  ⟹  (e1∘e2)=(e2∘e1)e_1 \perp e_2 \implies (e_1 \circ e_2) = (e_2 \circ e_1)e1​⊥e2​⟹(e1​∘e2​)=(e2​∘e1​)

If there is no causal path from e1e_1e1​ to e2e_2e2​ or from e2e_2e2​ to e1e_1e1​, then the order in which they are applied doesn't matter. The final state is the same either way.

This is physically motivated: if two events cannot influence each other, their relative ordering is not a fact about the world — it is a coordinate choice. Causal invariance encodes this.

Terminology note: In the derived spacetime geometry, causally disconnected events are called "spacelike-separated." We avoid that term here because spacetime has not yet been derived — we work only with causal structure.

Open problem: Does P2 follow from P1 alone, or does it require additional structure? See Cause-Plex and Spacetime for the current state of this question.

P3: Finite Minimum Event Latency

Every causal event has a latency τe≥τmin⁡>0\tau_e \geq \tau_{\min} > 0τe​≥τmin​>0:

∀e∈E:τe≥τmin⁡>0\forall e \in E: \tau_e \geq \tau_{\min} > 0∀e∈E:τe​≥τmin​>0

This defines a maximum propagation rate. The mechanism: if every causal event takes at least τmin⁡\tau_{\min}τmin​, then any causal influence must traverse at least one event per τmin⁡\tau_{\min}τmin​. When spacetime is derived from this causal structure (see Spacetime below), distance is measured in units of causal events — the minimum spatial interval ℓmin⁡\ell_{\min}ℓmin​ is the interval associated with one event step. The maximum propagation rate is then c=ℓmin⁡/τmin⁡c = \ell_{\min}/\tau_{\min}c=ℓmin​/τmin​. In the continuum limit where the discrete cause-plex structure becomes smooth spacetime, this ratio becomes the speed of light. Note that ℓmin⁡\ell_{\min}ℓmin​ is not assumed here — it is defined by the same causal structure that defines distance.

What Emerges

Given P1–P3, the structure of physics emerges:

Spacetime

What's established vs what's ours: The derivation of spacetime geometry from causal structure is not our contribution — it is established physics from causal set theory (Bombelli, Lee, Meyer, Sorkin 1987) and Malament's theorem (1977). Epimechanics builds on this foundation; it does not claim to have discovered it.

The Lorentzian metric — the geometry of special relativity — emerges from causal structure. Spacetime is not a container that events happen in; spacetime is the geometry of causal relationships. This is a proven result:

  • Malament's theorem (1977): The causal ordering uniquely determines the spacetime metric up to a conformal factor. This is established mathematics.
  • Causal set theory (Bombelli et al. 1987): The "number = volume" conjecture fixes the conformal factor via event counting. Well-supported but not proven.

What epimechanics adds: We extend this foundation upward — from Planck-scale causal events through the coarse-graining ladder to biology, cognition, and institutions. The spacetime derivation is the floor we stand on, not our ceiling.

See Cause-Plex and Spacetime for the full technical treatment.

Time

Time is not primitive. Time is the count of causal events along a path:

τ(γ)=∣{e∈γ}∣⋅τmin⁡\tau(\gamma) = |\{e \in \gamma\}| \cdot \tau_{\min}τ(γ)=∣{e∈γ}∣⋅τmin​

The "flow of time" is the accumulation of causal events. A clock is a stable causal loop that produces events at a regular rate. The second is defined by counting Cs-133 hyperfine transitions (9,192,631,770 per second by definition). All time measurements are ratios of cause-plex path counts.

Energy and Conserved Quantities

Energy is not primitive. It emerges from Noether's theorem: if the cause-plex has a continuous symmetry, there exists a conserved quantity.

Cause-plex symmetryConserved quantityName
Time-translation invariance∑ipiq˙i−L\sum_i p_i \dot{q}_i - L∑i​pi​q˙​i​−LEnergy
Spatial translation invariance∑imiq˙i\sum_i m_i \dot{q}_i∑i​mi​q˙​i​Momentum
Rotational invariance∑iri×pi\sum_i r_i \times p_i∑i​ri​×pi​Angular momentum
U(1) gauge symmetry∑iqi\sum_i q_i∑i​qi​Charge

Energy is what we call the conserved quantity when the cause-plex has time-translation symmetry. In regions where this symmetry holds (most of everyday physics), energy is well-defined and conserved. In regions where it is broken (strongly non-equilibrium, rapidly evolving, cosmological expansion), energy is not a clean quantity.

Units

Units are not primitive. They are ratios of cause-plex path counts to reference cause-plex path counts:

  • The second: 9,192,631,770 Cs-133 hyperfine transitions (by definition)
  • The meter: The distance light travels in 1/299,792,458 of a second
  • The kilogram: Defined via Planck's constant, the second, and the meter

All physical units reduce to counting causal events relative to reference causal events. No unit is assumed.

Quantum Mechanics

When multiple causal paths coexist — when the cause-plex has a multiway structure — quantum mechanics emerges.

What is multiway structure? A single causal event can have multiple possible outcomes. Instead of one path through the cause-plex, there are many — a branching tree of possibilities. The multiway cause-plex is the graph of all these paths, coexisting until some process (measurement, decoherence) selects among them.

How does QM emerge? Each path through the multiway cause-plex carries an amplitude — a complex number. When paths converge (lead to the same final state), their amplitudes interfere: they can add constructively or cancel destructively. The probability of observing a state is the squared magnitude of the total amplitude reaching it (the Born rule). The Schrödinger equation describes how amplitudes evolve as events accumulate.

This is the same insight as Feynman's path integral formulation: quantum mechanics is what happens when you sum over all possible histories. The cause-plex provides the structure; the amplitudes provide the weights; interference produces quantum behavior.

See Cause-Plex and Quantum Mechanics for the full derivation.

The Four-Layer Architecture

The Event Layer is the foundation of a four-layer architecture:

LayerContentWhat it is
Event LayerCausal event e:Si→Sje: \mathcal{S}_i \to \mathcal{S}_je:Si​→Sj​, cause-plex (E,≺)(E, \prec)(E,≺)The primitive — no physics assumed
Structure LayerBonds, loopsRecurring patterns in the cause-plex
Descriptor LayerQ1–Q5 structural propertiesHow to characterize bonds and loops
Observable LayerEnergy, mass, force, temperatureDerived quantities valid where symmetries hold

Each layer emerges from patterns in the layer below. The Event Layer is the foundation; everything else is emergent.

The key insight: quantities like energy and mass live at the Observable Layer, not the Event Layer. They are coarse-grained descriptions valid where certain symmetries hold. At biological and institutional scales, time-translation symmetry holds well enough that "energy" is the right concept. At the Planck scale or in strongly non-equilibrium systems, you may need to work at the Event Layer directly.

Relationship to Other Work

Causal Set Theory

Credit where due: The cause-plex IS causal set theory at the physics level. We do not claim to have discovered the causal approach to spacetime — that is the work of Bombelli, Sorkin, Malament, and others over 40+ years.

The cause-plex (E,≺)(E, \prec)(E,≺) is identical to a causal set as defined by Bombelli et al. 1987. The spacetime derivation (Malament's theorem, number=volume) is theirs. What epimechanics contributes is the extension — not the foundation:

Inherited from CST (established)Our proposal (untested)
Causal partial order as primitive—
Spacetime from causal structure—
Malament's theorem—
Number = volume conjecture—
Lorentz invariance derivation—
—Coarse-graining ladder to biology/society
—Q1-Q5 entity type descriptors
—Generalized mass, auto-causal density
—Observer-selection argument for 3+1D

The right column is a research program, not established results. The test: do these concepts generate measurable predictions? That's what the applications documents aim to develop.

Wolfram's Ruliad

The cause-plex is a specific subgraph of the ruliad — the one realized by the physical world. The ruliad derivation works from abstract update rules; the cause-plex derivation works from physical causal events. Both arrive at similar structure and face similar challenges: deriving specific predictions (particle masses, coupling constants) remains an open problem for both programs.

Process Philosophy

The cause-plex instantiates Whitehead's process ontology: events, not substances, are fundamental. What we call "things" are stable patterns in the flow of events.

What This Document Does Not Cover

This document establishes the Event Layer — the foundation. It does not cover:

  • How bonds and loops emerge from causal events → Part 1.5: Causors
  • The full derivation of spacetime → Cause-Plex and Spacetime
  • The full derivation of quantum mechanics → Cause-Plex and Quantum Mechanics
  • Why 3+1 dimensions → Cause-Plex Dimensionality
  • The mechanical grammar (mass, force, energy, coupling) → Part 1: Generalized Mechanics

Open Problems

The Event Layer framework inherits open problems from causal set theory and raises new ones:

OP1: Does P2 follow from P1? Causal invariance (P2) states that causally disconnected events commute. This is not arbitrary — it is the definition of "no causal connection": if the order mattered, there would be a causal path. The open question is whether this can be derived formally from P1 alone or requires stating as an independent axiom. Either way, P2 is not an additional physical assumption — it is what "causally disconnected" means.

OP2: The continuum limit. Taking a discrete cause-plex to continuous spacetime requires a measure, topology, and assumptions about event distribution. The derivation of Lorentz invariance in this limit is technically non-trivial and an active research area in causal set theory.

OP3: Quantum mechanics from multiway structure. The claim that complex amplitudes, the Born rule, and the Schrödinger equation emerge from multiway graph structure is a research program, not a completed derivation. The specific mechanism mapping path interference to probability amplitudes requires further development.

OP4: Selection of the physical cause-plex. What determines which events are "real" causal events? Without a selection criterion, "the cause-plex realized by the physical world" is circular. This is the analogue of Wolfram's ruliad selection problem.

OP5: Noether in the discrete. Applying Noether's theorem (which requires continuous symmetry and a differentiable action) to a discrete cause-plex requires technical work on the continuum limit that is not completed here.

These are honest acknowledgments of work remaining, not weaknesses to hide. The framework's value is in providing a unified conceptual architecture; the technical derivations are an ongoing research program.

Summary

The Event Layer is the foundation of epimechanics:

  1. The primitive is the causal event — a state transition e:Si→Sje: \mathcal{S}_i \to \mathcal{S}_je:Si​→Sj​

  2. The cause-plex is the hypergraph of all causal events — (E,≺)(E, \prec)(E,≺)

  3. Three properties generate physics:

    • P1: Causal partial ordering
    • P2: Causal invariance (causally disconnected events commute)
    • P3: Finite minimum event latency

  4. What emerges (credit: causal set theory, not us):

    • Spacetime from causal geometry — CST result (Malament 1977, Bombelli et al. 1987)
    • Time from event counts — CST framing (proper time as chain length)
    • Energy from symmetry — standard physics (Noether's theorem)
    • Lorentz invariance — CST result (causal structure → symmetry group)

  5. What epimechanics proposes (untested):

    • The coarse-graining ladder from Planck scale to institutions
    • Q1-Q5 entity descriptors and the causor taxonomy
    • Generalized mass and auto-causal density as domain-general quantities
    • Application to biology, cognition, economics

Be clear: The physics foundation is inherited. The multi-scale extension is a hypothesis. The test is empirical: do these concepts predict anything measurable? See applications for attempts to answer this.

content.html:
In plain English: The periodic table tells you what atoms are made of. This document asks the same question one level more general: what are entities made of — not just atoms, but any persistent thing? The answer: bonds (recurring causal connections) and loops (closed cycles of bonds that sustain themselves). Five structural questions — energy mode, output target, topology, leverage, and timescale — characterize any bond or loop. From these, you can predict what kind of entity it is. A flame, a cell, an institution — all are specific configurations of bonds and loops. The labels come last; the structure comes first.

The Periodic Table Problem

Part 1 defined the grammar of Epimechanics — how state XXX, force FFF, energy WWW, and coupling TijT^i{}_jTij​ relate. Two quantities emerged: generalized mass M\mathcal{M}M (total causal content) and auto-causal density ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​ (the self-sustaining fraction). The grammar works — you can model institutional inertia, belief persistence, metabolic dynamics. But M\mathcal{M}M and ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​ are still black boxes. What are they made of?

Chemistry had F=maF = maF=ma for two centuries before understanding what mass is made of. Epimechanics needs the same thing: the elements — the finite set of structural primitives that combine to produce the diversity of entities.

This document provides those elements: bonds and loops. Together, we call them causors — the causal structure primitives characterized by their position in Q1–Q5 parameter space. The causor framework is the vocabulary for reading what kind of entity you're looking at from its structural coordinates.

Where This Fits: The Four-Layer Architecture

Epimechanics has a four-layer architecture. This document covers the Structure Layer and Descriptor Layer:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  OBSERVABLE LAYER — Derived quantities                      │
│  Energy, mass, force, temperature                           │
│  (Valid where symmetries hold)                              │
│  → Part 1: Generalized Mechanics                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  DESCRIPTOR LAYER — Structural questions (Q1–Q5)            │
│  Energy mode, output target, topology, leverage, timescale  │
│  → This document (Section 3)                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  STRUCTURE LAYER — Structural primitives                    │
│  Bonds, Loops                                               │
│  → This document (Section 2)                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  EVENT LAYER — The primitive                                │
│  Causal events, cause-plex                                  │
│  → Part 0b: The Event Layer                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The Event Layer (Part 0b) defines the primitive: causal events and the cause-plex. This document builds on that foundation, showing how bonds and loops emerge as patterns in the cause-plex, and how the Q1–Q5 descriptors characterize them.

0. Worked Example: A Candle Flame Through All Four Layers

Before the formal definitions, here is a single system — a candle flame — described at each layer. This is what the architecture looks like in practice:

LayerFlame Description
Event LayerFour causal events: melting, vaporization, combustion, heat transfer. Each is a state transition e:Si→Sje: \mathcal{S}_i \to \mathcal{S}_je:Si​→Sj​ with no energy assumed — just "this configuration follows from that one."
Structure LayerThe four events form bonds (recurring causal patterns). The bonds compose into a closed loop: combustion produces heat, heat melts wax, melted wax vaporizes, vapor combusts. The loop regenerates its own conditions.
Descriptor LayerQ1: Kinetic (energy drives motion, not storage). Q2: Direct (bonds target state variables) + Enable (heat bond maintains the loop). Q3: Closed. Q4: Λ ≈ 1. Q5: Fast relative to observation timescale.
Observable LayerEnergy release ~40 kJ/g. Auto-causal density ρac>0\rho_{\text{ac}} > 0ρac​>0 (the loop sustains itself). Maintenance cost > 0 (requires continuous wax input). Temperature, luminosity, and combustion rate are all Observable Layer quantities derived from the underlying structure.

The flame is a dissipative auto-causal entity: it sustains itself by continuously processing fuel through a closed causal loop. Remove the fuel (wax), and the loop breaks — the flame goes out. The Observable Layer quantities (energy, temperature) are derived; the Structure Layer topology (closed loop) is what makes it auto-causal.

Note: This four-event decomposition makes heat transfer explicit. The three-event version in Part 0b collapses the heat→melt step to illustrate causal disconnection (P2). Both decompositions are valid at different granularities.

1. The Foundation: Events and the Cause-Plex

This section summarizes the Event Layer. For the full treatment, see Part 0b: The Event Layer.

The primitive is the causal event — a state transition:

e:Si→Sje: \mathcal{S}_i \to \mathcal{S}_je:Si​→Sj​

The cause-plex C=(E,≺)\mathcal{C} = (E, \prec)C=(E,≺) is the hypergraph of all causal events with their partial ordering. From the cause-plex's structure, spacetime, energy, and quantum mechanics emerge. Energy is not primitive — it is the conserved quantity that appears when the cause-plex has time-translation symmetry (Noether's theorem).

At scales where time-translation symmetry holds — which includes most of biology, economics, and social systems — "energy" is the right description. The Structure Layer builds on this: bonds and loops are patterns in the cause-plex that, at Observable Layer, appear as energy exchanges.

2. Structure Layer: Bonds and Loops

2.1 The Bond Operator

A bond is a recurring pattern of causal events: a persistent causal connection between state variables, where changes in XiX_iXi​ reliably produce changes in XjX_jXj​.

b:Xi⇉Xjb: X_i \rightrightarrows X_jb:Xi​⇉Xj​

The double arrow indicates: reliable, repeated, not one-off.

At the Observable Layer (where energy is defined), bonds appear as energy exchanges. At the Event Layer, a bond is a cluster of causal events with a stable statistical structure — the same transition pattern fires reliably across different instances.

Bond properties:

PropertySymbolMeaning
Directioni→ji \to ji→jAsymmetric in general
Strengthσb\sigma_bσb​Resistance to dissolution
Latencyτb\tau_bτb​Time between input and output
Reliabilityrb∈[0,1]r_b \in [0,1]rb​∈[0,1]Probability the pattern fires when activated (see §10: candidate for Q6)

Bond strength σb\sigma_bσb​ has two equivalent descriptions:

  • Observable Layer: The energy required to break the bond
  • Event Layer: The count of alternative causal sequences required to dissolve the pattern

Why these might be equivalent (hypothesis): If energy at the Event Layer is fundamentally the count of causal events (as proposed in Part 0b), then breaking a bond means redirecting causal flow — forcing the system through alternative sequences rather than the established pattern. The energy required to break the bond would equal the "causal work" of establishing those alternative paths. This equivalence is the framework's proposal, not established physics. Testing it requires measuring both quantities independently and checking agreement.

2.2 The Loop Operator

A loop is a closed composition of bonds — a causal cycle where the output of the last bond feeds back to the input of the first:

L:Xi⇉Xj⇉⋯⇉Xi\mathcal{L}: X_i \rightrightarrows X_j \rightrightarrows \cdots \rightrightarrows X_iL:Xi​⇉Xj​⇉⋯⇉Xi​

(Each ⇉\rightrightarrows⇉ denotes a bond, not a single causal event.)

Loops are the minimal structure for auto-causality. Individual bonds cannot be auto-causal (ρac=0\rho_{\text{ac}} = 0ρac​=0 for any single bond). The closed loop is the first level at which ρac>0\rho_{\text{ac}} > 0ρac​>0 can appear — the first level at which the cause-plex regenerates conditions for its own continuation.

Auto-causal does not mean self-contained. The Krebs cycle regenerates a key intermediate molecule (oxaloacetate) while requiring continuous fuel input (acetyl-CoA) and exporting waste (CO₂, electrons). Cut the input, the loop stops. Auto-causality is about loop regeneration, not independence from environment.

3. Descriptor Layer: The Five Structural Questions

Every bond and loop forces five structural questions. These are continuous parameters, not binary categories. Together they characterize any causal structure.

Q1: Energy Mode

Where does received energy go?

mode(b)∈[kinetic, potential]\text{mode}(b) \in [\text{kinetic},\ \text{potential}]mode(b)∈[kinetic, potential]

ModeEffectExample
KineticIncreases state velocity X˙\dot{X}X˙Heat flow, kinetic impact
PotentialStored in configurationChemical bond, compressed spring

What we commonly call "structural bonds" are potential-mode bonds. Kinetic-mode bonds drive state change; potential-mode bonds resist it.

Q2: Output Target

What does the bond connect to?

TargetRoleEffect
State variable XjX_jXj​DirectState changes at output
Another bond b′b'b′GatingSmall event triggers large event
A loop L\mathcal{L}LEnableMaintains a transducer's existence

Gating is what "signal" describes at Observable Layer: a small bond cluster whose output triggers a much larger cluster from local reserves. Leverage ratio Λ=Pout/Pin≫1\Lambda = \mathcal{P}_{\text{out}} / \mathcal{P}_{\text{in}} \gg 1Λ=Pout​/Pin​≫1.

Enable is a bond whose output maintains a loop's existence — keeps a transducer alive. A transducer is an entity whose primary function is converting inputs of one type into outputs of another type (food → motion, light → signal, money → goods). At the Observable Layer: food → organism metabolism.

Q3: Topology

Open or closed?

topology∈[open chain, closed loop]\text{topology} \in [\text{open chain},\ \text{closed loop}]topology∈[open chain, closed loop]

Open chains propagate and dissipate. Closed loops can regenerate. ρac>0\rho_{\text{ac}} > 0ρac​>0 is a topological property of the cause-plex structure.

Q4: Leverage Ratio

How much amplification?

Λ=output event cluster sizeinput event cluster size\Lambda = \frac{\text{output event cluster size}}{\text{input event cluster size}}Λ=input event cluster sizeoutput event cluster size​

What bounds a cluster? An event cluster is the set of causal events triggered by an input within a specified causal horizon — typically one loop period or one bond latency. The boundary is set by the timescale of interest: for a synapse, the cluster is all events between neurotransmitter release and postsynaptic potential; for a gene regulatory bond, the cluster is all events between transcription factor binding and protein production. The cluster is operationally defined by the bond's characteristic timescale τb\tau_bτb​.

ValueTypeMeaning
Λ≈1\Lambda \approx 1Λ≈1SymmetricOutput matches input
Λ≫1\Lambda \gg 1Λ≫1GatingSmall input, large output from reservoir
Λ≪1\Lambda \ll 1Λ≪1LossyMost input dissipates before output

Q5: Timescale

How fast relative to the loop period?

Every bond has latency τb\tau_bτb​. In a loop, the ratio of bond latencies determines role:

  • Fast (τb≪Tloop\tau_b \ll T_{\text{loop}}τb​≪Tloop​): Regulator — responds quickly to perturbations
  • Slow (τb∼Tloop\tau_b \sim T_{\text{loop}}τb​∼Tloop​): Structural — sets the loop's characteristic timescale

Q5 is derived from Event Layer structure: it is the count of causal events per reference loop cycle, projected onto a reference clock.

4. From Structure to Entity Types

Stable configurations cluster at recognizable poles in the Q1–Q5 parameter space. These are the entity types we observe:

Each row is a region in a continuous parameter space. Real entities are intermediate and have mixed subsystems.

Loops-of-loops example: A cell has two core loops: (1) metabolism — the Krebs cycle and related pathways that regenerate ATP, and (2) replication — DNA copying, protein synthesis, and cell division that reproduce the metabolic machinery. Neither loop alone is an organism. The organism emerges when these loops are coupled: metabolism provides the energy and materials for replication; replication produces new copies of the metabolic machinery. This coupling forms a loop-of-loops — a higher-order structure where each component loop enables the other. Institutions have the same architecture: a company's operations loop (producing goods) and its HR loop (reproducing skilled workers) are coupled into a meta-entity that persists beyond any individual employee or product.

What Q1–Q5 tell you together: These five descriptors let you read a bond or loop and predict what kind of entity it belongs to — without invoking labels like "organism" or "institution." A bond that stores energy (Q1: potential), gates a larger cluster (Q2: gating), sits in a closed loop (Q3: closed), has high leverage (Q4: Λ ≫ 1), and fires slowly relative to the loop (Q5: slow) is behaving like a metabolic regulation step. A bond that dissipates energy (Q1: kinetic), connects directly to state (Q2: direct), is open-ended (Q3: open), and is low-leverage (Q4: Λ ≈ 1) is behaving like heat flow. The labels are summaries of structural configurations. The structure comes first.

5. Self-Containment Is a Spectrum

Self-containment is not binary. It is tied to the ratio of bond dissolution energy to thermal fluctuation energy:

The regime that epimechanics targets is where σb/kBT\sigma_b / k_BTσb​/kB​T is low enough that bonds degrade measurably, and loops are required to maintain structure.

At the Observable Layer, structural primitives aggregate into familiar quantities:

M=∑σb\mathcal{M} = \sum \sigma_bM=∑σb​ follows from the definition of generalized mass as total causal content: each bond contributes its strength (resistance to dissolution) to the entity's total inertia. This is not a metaphor — it is the same logic by which physical mass equals the sum of constituent particle masses. The domain-specific question is not whether this aggregation holds, but how to measure σb\sigma_bσb​ in each domain (bond dissociation energy in chemistry, switching cost in economics, belief revision difficulty in cognition). The grammar is universal; the measurement is domain-specific.

Dimensional analysis: In the mechanical grammar, p=MX˙p = \mathcal{M}\dot{X}p=MX˙, so [M]=[p]/[X˙][\mathcal{M}] = [p]/[\dot{X}][M]=[p]/[X˙]. For abstract state spaces (beliefs, market positions), XXX is dimensionless or has domain-specific units, and M\mathcal{M}M inherits corresponding dimensions. In chemistry, σb\sigma_bσb​ is bond dissociation energy (Joules); M\mathcal{M}M then has dimensions of energy, and the Lagrangian L=12M∣X˙∣2−VL = \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{M}|\dot{X}|^2 - VL=21​M∣X˙∣2−V requires X˙\dot{X}X˙ to be dimensionless (a rate of change in a normalized state space). 7. Causal Attack Surface

High ρac\rho_{\text{ac}}ρac​ has a dual character. The same loops that sustain an entity become amplification engines if a keystone bond is perturbed. Define:

For a cell, ∂E\partial E∂E includes membrane transport proteins; for an institution, ∂E\partial E∂E includes customer-facing processes and supply chain bonds.

The entity's auto-causal power becomes the propagation mechanism for its own dissolution.

8. Connections

Assembly Theory

Assembly theory (Cronin & Walker 2023) counts the minimum bond-formation operations to construct an object — the assembly index. The causor framework extends this:

  1. Typed bonds. Assembly index counts undifferentiated operations; Q1–Q5 track bond structure
  2. Construction to maintenance. Assembly index measures build complexity; CmaintC_{\text{maint}}Cmaint​ measures keep complexity
  3. Static to dynamic. Assembly index is a snapshot; the cause-plex tracks evolution, degradation, repair

Representational Efficiency

The right description level is where state variables correspond to natural clusters of bonds with stable dynamics. This is coarse-graining: identify mesoscale structures (phonons, metabolic cycles, institutional processes) that capture behavior more efficiently than tracking individual events. The cause-plex provides the substrate; the Representational Efficiency principle selects the right level.

The periodic table of chemistry gives you elements. The causor framework gives you structural primitives. From bonds and loops characterized by Q1–Q5, you can derive what kind of entity you're looking at — without assuming labels.

10. How to Use This (If You Want to Test It)

The Q1-Q5 framework is untested. Here's how you could apply it:

  1. Pick a system you understand well (a metabolic pathway, a market mechanism, an organizational process)
  2. Identify the bonds — what are the recurring causal connections? What changes what?
  3. Characterize each bond by Q1-Q5:
    • Q1: Does it store energy or dissipate it?
    • Q2: Does it connect to state directly, gate another bond, or enable a loop?
    • Q3: Is it part of a closed loop or an open chain?
    • Q4: What's the leverage ratio (output/input)?
    • Q5: Fast or slow relative to the system's characteristic timescale?
  4. Check predictions: Does the entity-type table (§4) correctly predict what kind of system you're looking at?
  5. Report failures: Where does the framework get it wrong? That's the valuable data.

The test: Does Q1-Q5 classification tell you something you didn't already know? If not, it's relabeling. If yes, what?

11. Open Questions

Q1: Are Q1–Q5 complete? Can every distinction between causal structures be captured by position in the Q1–Q5 parameter space? Candidate additional dimensions: spatial locality, stochasticity (related to bond reliability rbr_brb​), thermodynamic reversibility.

Q2: CI and stability. High complexity may correlate with deep stability basins — but need not (fragile complexity). What is the formal relationship between construction complexity and thermodynamic stability?
